BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r1.claim: The Prophet received knowledge without learning to write and became a source of knowledge about writing, its rules, and crafts; God knows what is manifest and hidden.
BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r1.anchor: من غير تعلم الخط وكان منبع الكمالات كلها حتى إنه علم الكتاب الخط وقوانينه

BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r2.claim: God lets the Prophet forget what should be forgotten and preserves what should remain, according to the interests of religion.
BURSEVI:v10p315#2/r2.anchor: فينسى ما يشاء إنساءه ويبثقى محفوظا ما يشاء إبقاءه

SULAMI:v2p389#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p389#5/r1.speaker: محمد بن حامد
SULAMI:v2p389#5/r1.claim: God knows charity whether it is concealed or openly given.
SULAMI:v2p389#5/r1.anchor: قال محمد بن حامد : يعلم إخفاء الصدقة وإعلانها

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#5/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#5/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#5/r1.claim: Qatada says the Prophet forgot nothing except what God willed and glosses what is hidden as inner whispering.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#5/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : سنقرئك فلا تنسى الا ما شاء الله قال : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا ينسى شيئا الا ما شاء الله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#5/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#5/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#5/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says what is hidden is what a person conceals within himself.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#5/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير انه يعلم الجهر وما يخفى قال : ما اخفيت في نفسك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#4/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#4/r1.claim: One view makes the exception mean whatever God wills to abrogate, so that the Prophet then forgets it; this is reported from al-Ḥasan and Qatāda.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#4/r1.anchor: أحدها إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسخه فتنساه قاله الحسن وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#4/r2.claim: A second view allows God to will that the Prophet forget something, likening the phrasing to the exception in 11:107; the passage says that He will not will it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#4/r2.anchor: والثاني إلا ما شاء الله أن تنسى شيئا فإنما هو كقوله تعالى خالدين فيها ما دامت السموات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#4/r3.claim: God knows what is spoken and done openly and what is hidden from both.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#4/r3.anchor: من القول والفعل وما يخفى منهما

KASHSHAF:87:7/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:7/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:7/r1.claim: Except what God wills means He removes it from memory by abrogating its ruling and recitation, as in the cited verse.
KASHSHAF:87:7/r1.anchor: فذهب به عن حفظه برفع حكمه وتلاوته

KASHSHAF:87:7/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:7/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:7/r2.claim: Another explanation says the Prophet hurried while Gabriel recited; he was told not to hurry, since Gabriel would repeat it until he memorized it and would not forget except by God's will.
KASHSHAF:87:7/r2.anchor: كان يعجل بالقراءة إذا لقنه جبريل

KASHSHAF:87:7/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:7/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:7/r3.claim: An exception can mean only a rare lapse: a report says the Prophet omitted a verse in prayer, and Ubayy thought it abrogated until the Prophet said he had forgotten it.
KASHSHAF:87:7/r3.anchor: أنه أسقط آية في قراءته في الصلاة

KASHSHAF:87:7/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:7/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:7/r4.claim: The exception may rhetorically deny forgetting altogether, using a very small exception to mean negation, as in the speaker's example to a friend.
KASHSHAF:87:7/r4.anchor: والغرض نفى النسيان رأساً كما يقول الرجل لصاحبه أنت سهيمي فيما أملك

KASHSHAF:87:7/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:7/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:7/r5.claim: Alternatively, fa-la tansa is a prohibition, with an extra alif for rhyme; do not neglect recitation and repetition, except if God wills its recitation abrogated for a purpose.

KASHSHAF:87:7/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:7/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:7/r6.claim: God knows the Prophet's aloud reading alongside Gabriel and his fear of losing the recitation, and reassures him that He will protect it.
KASHSHAF:87:7/r6.anchor: يعني أنك تجهر بالقراءة مع قراءة جبريل عليه السلام مخافة التفلت

KASHSHAF:87:7/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:7/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:7/r7.claim: Alternatively, God knows what people conceal and disclose and what benefits or harms their religion, so He abrogates some revelation and leaves other parts preserved.
KASHSHAF:87:7/r7.anchor: أو يعلم ما أسررتم وما أعلنتم من أقوالكم وأفعالكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r5.claim: God knowing the loud and hidden may reassure the Prophet who recited aloud alongside Gabriel from fear of forgetting; alternatively it covers all hidden and public states and God's choices about what to erase or preserve.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p740#2/r5.anchor: والله يعلم جهرك معه وما في نفسك مما يدعوك إلى الجهر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#7/r1.claim: The exception means what God chooses to abrogate: God assures the Prophet that revelation will remain preserved except what He removes from memory by lifting its ruling and recitation.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#7/r1.anchor: أن ينسخه وهذا بشارة من الله لبنيه أن يحفظ عليه الوحى حتى لا ينفلت منه شئ

NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#7/r2.speaker: جنيد
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#7/r2.claim: When Ibn Kaysan asked Junayd about “you will not forget,” Junayd interpreted it as not forgetting to act upon the revelation.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#7/r2.anchor: وسأل ابن كيسان النحوى جنيدا عنه فقال فلا تنسى العمل به

NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#7/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#7/r3.claim: Another reading treats “you will not forget” as a prohibition, with an added final alif for rhyme; it means do not repeat the recitation until you forget it, except what God causes you to forget by lifting its recitation.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#7/r3.anchor: وقيل قوله فلا تنسى على النهى والألف مزيدة للفاصلة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#7/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#7/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#7/r4.claim: God knows the Prophet's audible recitation alongside Gabriel and the inward fear of forgetting; alternatively He knows hidden and public speech, deeds, and states.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#7/r4.anchor: أى إنك تجهر بالقراءة مع قراءة جبريل مخافة التفلت والله يعلم جهرك معه وما فى نفسك

QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r1.claim: The exception means God may cause the Prophet to forget recitation by lifting its recitation for a benefit; the author prefers this because the exception from a prohibition is normally temporary and the yāʾ appears in every codex and reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r1.anchor: والأول هو المختار لأن الاستثناء من النهي لا يكاد يكون إلا مؤقتا معلوما

QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r3.claim: God knows public speech and action and concealed secrets; Ibn ʿAbbas says He knows what is in the heart and self.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r3.anchor: قوله تعالى: { إنه يعلم الجهر } أي الإعلان من القول والعمل. { وما يخفى } من السر.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r4.speaker: محمد بن حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r4.claim: Muhammad ibn Hatim interprets the known public and hidden matters as charity given openly or secretly.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r5.claim: Another interpretation makes the loud what the Prophet memorized in his breast and the hidden what was erased from it.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:7-8/r5.anchor: وقيل: الجهر ما حفظته من القرآن في صدرك. «وما يخفى» هو ما نسخ من صدرك.

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.claim: Al-Aʿla is Meccan and has nineteen verses; the Prophet loved it, recited it at Eid and Friday prayers with al-Ghashiya, sometimes on the same day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.anchor: سورة الأعلى مكية وآياتها تسع عشرة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.claim: The surah turns the entire cosmos into a sanctuary reverberating with praise and offers the Prophet good news of divine preservation and ease in his mission and affairs.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.anchor: وحق لرسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أن يحب هذه السورة وهي تحيل له الكون كله معبدا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.claim: Its foundations are God's oneness as creator, divine revelation, and afterlife recompense, rooted in earlier scriptures; it also portrays the easy nature of the message, messenger, and community.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.anchor: وهي تتضمن الثابت من قواعد التصور الإيماني

QUTB-ZILAL:87:7/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:7/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:7/r1.claim: The exception “unless God wills” preserves the unrestricted divine will even after the promise of preservation, keeping hearts continually attached to that will.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:7/r1.anchor: فهو الاحتراس الذي يقرر طلاقة المشيئة الإلهية

QUTB-ZILAL:87:7/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:7/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:7/r2.claim: God's knowledge of what is public and hidden explains the preceding preservation and exception: His decisions follow wisdom informed by full knowledge of every aspect.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:7/r2.anchor: وكأن هذا تعليل لما مر في هذا المقطع من الإقرار والحفظ والاستثناء

RAZI:87:7/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:7/r1.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI:87:7/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says the Prophet forgot nothing after this verse descended.
RAZI:87:7/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي : إنه عليه السلام لم ينس بعد نزول هذه الآية شيئا

RAZI:87:7/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:7/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:87:7/r2.claim: On the nonliteral-exception reading, the phrase may teach blessing by saying “if God wills,” as God does even while knowing all outcomes.
RAZI:87:7/r2.anchor: فأنت وأمتك يا محمد أولى بها

RAZI:87:7/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:7/r3.speaker: الفراء
RAZI:87:7/r3.claim: Al-Farra says God did not will the Prophet to forget; the exception only declares that God could make him forget if He chose.
RAZI:87:7/r3.anchor: قال الفراء : إنه تعالى ما شاء أن ينسى محمد عليه السلام شيئا

RAZI:87:7/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:7/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:87:7/r4.claim: This hypothetical exception teaches that the Prophet’s not forgetting is God’s grace and kindness, not his own power.
RAZI:87:7/r4.anchor: فائدة هذا الاستثناء أن الله تعالى يعرفه قدرة ربه حتى يعلم أن عدم النسيان

RAZI:87:7/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:7/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:87:7/r5.claim: Mentioning the exception kept the Prophet alert and careful with every revelation, since any amount might have been excepted.
RAZI:87:7/r5.anchor: جوز رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في كل ما ينزل عليه من الوحي

RAZI:87:7/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:7/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:87:7/r6.claim: The exception may simply negate forgetting altogether, as in an idiom that adds an exception without intending to exclude anything.
RAZI:87:7/r6.anchor: أن يكون الغرض من قوله : { إلا ما شاء الله } نفي النسيان رأسا

RAZI:87:7/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:7/r7.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI:87:7/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads a real exception: the Prophet might temporarily forget and then remember, without permanent total forgetting.
RAZI:87:7/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج : إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسى ، فإنه ينسى ثم يتذكر بعد ذلك

RAZI:87:7/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:7/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:87:7/r8.claim: A report says the Prophet omitted a verse while praying; Ubay thought it had been abrogated, but the Prophet said he had forgotten it.
RAZI:87:7/r8.anchor: فحسب أبي أنها نسخت ، فسأله فقال : نسيتها

RAZI:87:7/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:7/r9.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI:87:7/r9.claim: Muqatil interprets forgetting as abrogation: God may withdraw a verse and command that it no longer be recited or prayed with.
RAZI:87:7/r9.anchor: فيأمرك أن لا تقرأه ولا تصلي به

RAZI:87:7/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:7/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:87:7/r10.claim: A real exception could mean rare minor lapses, but not forgetting religious obligations, which would damage the law and is impermissible.
RAZI:87:7/r10.anchor: ويشترط أن لا يكون ذلك القليل من واجبات الشرع

RAZI:87:7/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:7/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:87:7/r11.claim: “He knows what is public and hidden” may mean God knows the Prophet’s audible recitation with Gabriel and his private fear, and will relieve it.
RAZI:87:7/r11.anchor: وعالم بالسر الذي في قلبك وهو أنك تخاف النسيان

RAZI:87:7/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:7/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:87:7/r12.claim: Alternatively, the Prophet forgets only what God wills to abrogate, since God knows where abrogation serves people’s interests.
RAZI:87:7/r12.anchor: أن ينسخ ، فإنه أعلم بمصالح العبيد

SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r1.claim: One analysis makes the exception refer to what God wills the Prophet to forget, namely recitation being lifted; a report says he would awaken having forgotten verses, linked to 2:106.
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنه مفرغ، أي: إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسيكه فإنك تنساه.

SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r2.claim: Another view takes the exception to indicate rare occurrence: the Prophet once omitted a verse in prayer, and Ubayy thought it abrogated until told it was forgotten.
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r2.anchor: وقيل: إن المعنى بذلك القلة والندرة، كما روي

SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī, preceded by al-Farrāʾ and Makkī, reads the exception as rhetorical minimization meaning complete denial of forgetting, not a real exception.
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " الغرض نفي النسيان رأسا، كما يقول الرجل لصاحبه:

SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r4.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and others call the exception a conventional filler with nothing actually excepted; the Shaykh objects that such a claim is unsuitable in divine or eloquent speech.
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء وجماعة معه: " هذا الاستثناء صلة في الكلام على سنة الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r5.claim: The filler analysis need not mean sheer redundancy: its intended force is emphatic denial of forgetting or a prohibition against it.
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r5.anchor: أي: زائدا محضا بل المعنى الذي ذكره، وهو المبالغة في نفي النسيان

SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r6.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r6.claim: Makkī says God does not will the Prophet to forget anything, comparing the exception to the two Hūd passages without any actual reduction of eternity.
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r6.anchor: وقيل: معنى ذلك، إلا ما شاء الله، وليس يشاء الله أن ينسى منه شيئا

SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r7.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r7.claim: Makkī also transmits an exception from the making of dark detritus, but the author says this analysis is categorically impermissible.
SAMIN-DURR:87:7/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو استثناء من قوله { فجعله غثآء أحوى }. نقله مكي.

SAMIN-DURR:87:7#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:7#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:7#2/r1.claim: Mā yakhfā is a substantive pronoun; a verbal-noun reading would leave the verb without a subject, though that reading would otherwise coordinate more neatly with an explicit verbal noun.
SAMIN-DURR:87:7#2/r1.anchor: " ما " اسمية. ولا يجوز أن تكون مصدرية لئلا يلزم خلو الفعل من فاعل.

STUDYQURAN:87:7/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:7/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:7/r1.claim: The Prophet's forgetting of a verse is by God's will, not a fault of his.
STUDYQURAN:87:7/r1.anchor: because God willed it, not because of a fault on the part of the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:87:7/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:7/r2.speaker: Muslims
STUDYQURAN:87:7/r2.claim: Muslims believe God abrogated some verses and caused others to be forgotten, replacing them with better verses.
STUDYQURAN:87:7/r2.anchor: Muslims believe that God abrogated some verses and caused others to be “forgotten,”

TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r7.claim: One interpretation says God informs the Prophet that He will teach and preserve the Qurʾān, while telling him not to rush its recitation.
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r7.anchor: فقال بعضهم: هذا إخبار من الله نبيه عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه يعلمه هذا القرآن، ويحفظه عليه، ونهي منه أن يعجل بقراءته

TAB-FULL:v24p315/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r1.speaker: قائلو هذه المقالة
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r1.claim: This interpretation reads the exception as allowing God to cause the Prophet to forget what He abrogates, removing its ruling and recitation.
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r1.anchor: فقال قائلو هذه المقالة: معنى الاستثناء في هذا الموضع على النسيان، ومعنى الكلام: فلا تنسى، إلا ما شاء الله أن تنساه

TAB-FULL:v24p315/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r2.claim: Mujāhid says the Prophet would rehearse the Qurʾān within himself from fear of forgetting it.
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: " {سنقرئك فلا تنسى} [سورة:] قال: كان يتذكر القرآن في نفسه مخافة أن ينسى "

TAB-FULL:v24p315/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r3.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet forgot nothing except what God willed him to forget.
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، " {سنقرئك فلا تنسى} كان صلى الله عليه وسلم لا ينسى شيئا {إلا ما شاء الله} [الأنعام: 128] "

TAB-FULL:v24p315/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r4.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r4.claim: Another interpretation reads forgetting as leaving Qurʾānic practice, except where God abrogates a ruling.
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى النسيان في هذا الموضع: الترك؛ وقالوا: معنى الكلام: سنقرئك يا محمد فلا تترك العمل بشيء منه

TAB-FULL:v24p315/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r5.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r5.claim: Some grammarians say God did not will the Prophet to forget anything; the exception is an idiomatic oath-like formula whose intent is to give everything requested.
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r5.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية يقول في ذلك: لم يشأ الله أن تنسى شيئا، وهو كقوله: {خالدين فيها ما دامت السموات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك}

TAB-FULL:v24p315/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r6.claim: Ṭabarī prefers that the exception means God may cause the Prophet to forget through abrogation and removal, judging this the clearest sense.
TAB-FULL:v24p315/r6.anchor: والقول الذي هو أولى بالصواب عندي، قول من قال: معنى ذلك: فلا تنسى إلا أن نشاء نحن أن ننسيكه بنسخه ورفعه.

TAB-FULL:v24p316/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p316/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p316/r1.claim: The admonition ends by warning Muhammad to avoid acting contrary to what God has permitted.
TAB-FULL:v24p316/r1.anchor: أحوالك بغير الذي أذن لك به

TABRISI:87:7-9/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9/r13.speaker: الحسن، قتادة
TABRISI:87:7-9/r13.claim: They take the exception as God willing to abrogate the ruling and recitation, so the Prophet need not retain what is abrogated.
TABRISI:87:7-9/r13.anchor: إلا ما شاء الله أن تنساه برفع حكمه وتلاوته هو قول الحسن وقتادة

TABRISI:87:7/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r22.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7/r22.claim: The exception can mean God may cause the Prophet to forget what He abrogates in ruling and recitation; this is a kind of abrogation.
TABRISI:87:7/r22.anchor: وعلى هذا فالإنشاء نوع من النسخ وقد مر بيانه في سورة البقرة عند قوله

TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r1.claim: The exception may mean that God delays sending down a passage, so the Prophet has not yet recited it.
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r1.anchor: معناه إلا ما شاء الله أن يؤخر إنزاله عليك فلا تقرأه

TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats the exception as a conventional qualification: God did not will the Prophet to forget anything, like the exception in 11:108.
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r2.anchor: لم يشأ الله أن ينسى عليه السلام شيئا فهو كقوله

TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r3.claim: The exception affirms the Prophet's distinction: though unlettered, he retained long Qurʾānic passages after a single recitation, proving prophetic inimitability.
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r3.anchor: ففي الآية بيان لفضيلة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وإخبار أنه مع كونه صلى الله عليه وسلم أميا كان يحفظ القرآن

TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r4.claim: God knows what is public and hidden, preserving for the Prophet what he wishes to retain whether spoken aloud or concealed.
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r4.anchor: معناه أن الله سبحانه يعلم العلانية والسر

TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7-9#2/r5.claim: Jahr is raised voice, opposite of whispering.

ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r1.speaker: classical commentators
ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r1.claim: Classical commentators take the passage as addressed to Muhammad and promise that he will remember the Qur'an except what God wills him to forget.
ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r1.anchor: The classical commentators assume that the above words are addressed specifically to the Prophet

ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r2.claim: Asad rejects the commentators' strained explanations of why God might make His messenger forget revealed Qur'an, especially the appeal to abrogation.
ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r2.anchor: many unconvincing explanations have been advanced from very early times down to our own days

ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r3.claim: Asad reads the address to Muhammad as also directed to humanity generally, linking it to the opening revelation in 96:1–5, especially the teaching of knowledge in 96:3–5.
ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r3.anchor: the above passage, though ostensibly addressed to the Prophet, is directed at man in general

ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r4.claim: The passage describes cumulative empirical and rational knowledge transmitted across generations and civilizations; God lets humanity acquire and share it, while obsolete learning may be forgotten as experience expands.
ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r4.anchor: mankind's cumulative acquisition of empirical and rational knowledge, handed down from generation to generation

ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r5.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r5.claim: Observation and speculation remain valuable but limited and cannot alone disclose ultimate truths.
ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n4/r5.anchor: all knowledge arrived at through our observation of the external world and through speculation

ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n5/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n5/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n5/r1.claim: Al-ghayb is what lies beyond human perception; because human knowledge is always incomplete, people need revelation to find their way through life.
ASAD-NOTES:87:6#n5/r1.anchor: all that is intrinsically beyond the reach of human perception (al-ghayb)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r1.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r1.claim: God may cause Muhammad to forget some recitation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r1.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: إلا ما شاء الله أن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r2.claim: The exception allows God to cause Muhammad to forget part of the recitation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r2.anchor: ونحوه قال مقاتل: إلا ما شاء الله أن تنسى منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r3.speaker: الحسن، قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r3.claim: The exception refers to what God abrogates by removing its ruling and recitation; causing forgetfulness is a kind of abrogation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r3.anchor: والإنساء (¬9) نوع من النسخ، (وهذا معنى قول الحسن (¬10)، وقتادة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r4.claim: God retains the right to make an exception in all things, but Muhammad forgot nothing after this verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي - {إلا ما شاء الله} استثناء منه، وله الاستثناء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r5.claim: Al-Farra says God did not will Muhammad to forget anything; the exception is a conventional reservation like the wording of an oath, with no intent to withhold.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r5.anchor: واختاره الفراء، فقال: لم يشأ أن ينسى شيئا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r6.speaker: أبو إسحق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r6.claim: God may let Muhammad forget something and later remind him; this is not complete, permanent forgetting.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p439/r6.anchor: قال أبو إسحق: إلا ما شاء الله، ثم يذكره بعد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p440/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p440/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p440/r1.claim: God knows public and private speech and action, including Muhammad’s audible recitation to Gabriel and the recitation he conceals from fear of forgetting.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p440/r1.anchor: يعلم العلانية، والسر. وهذا يتصل بما قبله على معنى يعلم

WAHIDI-QT:87:7/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:7/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:87:7/r1.claim: The exception refers to what God wills to abrogate.
WAHIDI-QT:87:7/r1.anchor: إلا ما شاء الله } أن ينسخه

WAHIDI-QT:87:7/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:7/r2.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-QT:87:7/r2.claim: Another reading takes the exception as God's willing, though He does not will the Prophet to forget.
WAHIDI-QT:87:7/r2.anchor: وقيل الا ما شاء الله وهولايشاء أن تنسى

WAHIDI-QT:87:7/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:7/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:87:7/r3.claim: God knows what is spoken and done openly, as well as what is concealed.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r1.claim: The exception is what God wills to abrogate from the recitation or its retention.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r1.anchor: إلا ما شاء الله } أن ينسخه.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r2.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r2.claim: An alternative reads the exception as what God wills, while affirming that He does not will that the Prophet forget.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r2.anchor: وقيل: إلا ما شاء الله، وهو لا يشاء أن تنسى

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r3.claim: God knows what is spoken and done openly, and what is concealed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:7-16/r3.anchor: إنه يعلم الجهر } من القول والفعل

ELMALILI:87:7-13/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r1.claim: God knows every outward and hidden state of people, so his promise to teach and preserve revelation is grounded in complete knowledge and merits trust and glorification.
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r1.anchor: Şüphesiz ki O, Allah, cehri de bilir gizliyi de her şeyden

ELMALILI:87:7-13/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r2.claim: Alternatively, the verse means God knows what is recited aloud and secretly; the Prophet should recite openly or privately as appropriate and act without forgetting.
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r2.anchor: yüksek sesle okunanı da bilir, gizli okunanı da.

ELMALILI:87:7-13/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r3.claim: The clause is parenthetical and is also grammatically attached to the promise that the Prophet will be made to recite.
ELMALILI:87:7-13/r3.anchor: Bu cümle mu‘terizadır. Şu da سَنُقْرِئُكَ’ye ma‘tuftur.

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:7:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:7:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:7:anmerkung/r1.claim: For the divine name Allāh, the note refers readers to the discussion at Q 95:8.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:7:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zum Gottesnamen Allāh vgl. die Anmerkung zu 95:8

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#5/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#5/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses what is hidden as inner whispering.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#5/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ يعلم الجهر وما يخفى ﴾ قال الوسوسه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r1.claim: The exception is from all objects: the Prophet will remember what is recited to him except what God wills him to forget; Hasan, Qatada, and others say this refers to abrogation of both ruling and recitation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r1.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما وهذا مما قضى الله تعالى نسخه وأن يرتفع حكمه وتلاوته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r2.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats forgetting as an allusion to God's lifting a verse's ruling and recitation, since what is withdrawn is left and eventually forgotten; Alusi sees no need for this figurative reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r2.anchor: وفي الكشاف أي إلا ما شاء الله فذهب به عن حفظك برفع حكمه وتلاوته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r3.claim: Lifting a ruling or recitation can ordinarily cause people to stop reciting and remembering a verse, or can explain why God removes it from the Prophet's memory, so the causal language needs no strained interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r3.anchor: والمراد إما بيان السبب العادي البعيد للذهاب الله تعالى به عن الحفظ

ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r4.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r4.claim: Aisha reports that ten known sucklings were recited and then abrogated by five known sucklings; abrogation does not mean the Prophet forgot every such verse, since scholars retained some.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r4.anchor: أخرج الشيخان عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها كان فيما أنزل عشر رضعات معلومات فنسخن بخمس معلومات

ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r5.claim: One explanation says the Prophet hurried while Gabriel dictated and was told to wait for repeated recitation; Alusi says the obligation to remember after forgetting is not established by this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r5.anchor: وقيل كان صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يعجل بالقراءة إذا لقنه جبريل عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r6.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r6.claim: A sound report says the Prophet omitted an āya while leading dawn prayer; Ubayy thought it had been abrogated, but the Prophet said he had forgotten it, and Alusi notes he would be reminded.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p105#2/r6.anchor: وقد جاء في صحيح البخاري وغيره أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أسقط آية في قراءته في الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r1.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r1.claim: Al-Farraʾ says God did not will that the Prophet forget anything, but the hypothetical exception shows divine power and teaches that his retention is God's favor; the possibility is known from elsewhere, including 20:114.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r1.anchor: فقال أنه تعالى ماشاء أن ينسى النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم شيئا إلا أن المقصود من الإستثناء بيان أنه تعالى لو أراد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r2.claim: The promise negates lasting, uncorrected forgetting, not every lapse; the Prophet is not left forgetful of essential law, while correction can come through revelation or a listener's reminder.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r2.anchor: ثم أن المراد من نفي نسيان شيء من القرآن نفي النسيان التام المستمر مما لا يقر عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r3.claim: Invoking God's name emphasizes awe and signals that the divine will, bearing all attributes, governs the exception.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r3.anchor: والألتفات إلى الأسم الجليل على سائر الأوجه لتربية المهابة والإيذان بدوران المشيئة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan links the promise to the Prophet's anxiety about forgetting while reciting to Gabriel; Alusi says a direct explanation or preparation for inspiration is more plausible.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r4.anchor: وقال أبو حيان أنه سبحانه لما أمره صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بالتسبيح

ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r5.claim: The clauses about divine knowledge can reinforce what precedes or what follows, or explain that God knows the Prophet's audible reading and fear and will preserve or let him forget what wisdom requires.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r5.anchor: إنه يعلم الجهر وما يخفى تعليل لما قبله والجهر هنا ما ظهر قولا أو فعلا أو غيرهما

ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r6.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r6.claim: Al-Farraʾ reads the exception as a statement that God could make the Prophet forget if He wished, although He did not; it teaches that perfect retention is a divine gift, supported by 17:86 and 20:114.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r6.anchor: وبالجملة ففائدة هذا الإستثناء أن يعرفه الله تعالى قدرته حتى يعلم صلى الله عليه وسلم أن عدم النسيان من فضله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r7.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects readings that make the exception merely hypothetical or a negation, judging them unfitting for God's speech; Alusi calls that rejection extreme.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r7.anchor: وأباهما غاية الإباء لعدم الوقوف على حقيقتهما

ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r8.speaker: الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r8.claim: Al-Razi says the Prophet is not allowed to remain forgetful of foundational law or duties, though he may be left to forget etiquette or sunnas.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r8.anchor: وقد ذكروا أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لا يقر على النسيان فيما كان من أصول الشرائع والواجبات

ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r9.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r9.claim: Abu Hayyan connects the promise of recitation and protection from forgetting to the preceding command to glorify, because reciting the revealed Qur'an is necessary to glorification; Alusi finds the link weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r9.anchor: وقال أبو حيان أنه سبحانه لما أمره صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بالتسبيح وكان لا يتم إلا بقراءة ما أنزل عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r10.claim: Alusi prefers treating “We shall make you recite” as an independent statement that explains why glorification is fitting or prepares the Prophet for divine inspiration, while signaling the blessing of glorification.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r10.anchor: ولو قيل أن سنقرئك استئناف واقع موقع التعليل للتسبيح أو للأمر به

ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r11.claim: “He knows what is open and hidden” explains God's management of recitation, preservation, and forgetting according to wisdom; other readings make it a general reinforcement or focus on the Prophet's audible recitation and anxiety.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r11.anchor: إنه يعلم الجهر وما يخفى تعليل لما قبله والجهر هنا ما ظهر قولا أو فعلا أو غيرهما

ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r12.claim: Alusi rejects attaching “He knows what is open and hidden” to the command to glorify as an explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p106/r12.anchor: وقيل إنه متعلق بقوله تعالى ( سبح اسم ربك الأعلى ) وهذا ليس بشيء كما ترى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r1.claim: God may make the Prophet forget a revelation by abrogating it, or display the Quran's power over even the greatest creature as a forgotten verse is later recalled.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r1.anchor: أن تنساه لأنه نسخه , أو لتظهر عظمته في أن أعظم الخلق يغلبه القرآن

BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r2.claim: God continuously knows public recitation and whatever is concealed, with the explicit pair showing both are equally within His knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p397/r2.anchor: يعلمه مطلقا لا بقيد كونه جهرا

ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r1.claim: The apparent reading takes the exception as intentional and substantive.

ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r2.claim: They take the exception as material God decreed to abrogate, removing its recitation and ruling.
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r2.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما : مما قضى الله نسخه

ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God may make the Prophet forget something so he can establish it as Sunnah; the Prophet says he forgets and is made to forget for that purpose.
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسيك

ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r4.claim: Another view allows a lapse that God later brings back to the Prophet's memory; a Prophetic report recalls verses brought to mind by ʿAbbād ibn Bishr's recitation.
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r4.anchor: وقيل : إلا ما شاء الله أن يغلبك النسيان عليه

ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r5.claim: Another explanation takes فلا تنسى as not abandoning practice, except where God wills to abrogate the ruling.
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r5.anchor: وقيل : { فلا تنسى } : أي فلا تترك العمل به

ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r6.speaker: الفراء وجماعة
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r6.claim: They call the exception a conventional filler with no actual matter excepted, following an Arab usage.
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء وجماعة : هذا استثناء صلة في الكلام

ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī adopts this view to deny forgetting altogether, using a small exception formula as negation, like calling someone one's partner in all property except what God wills.

ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Farrāʾ and al-Zamakhsharī because their account makes the exception no exception, unsuitable even in eloquent speech.
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r8.anchor: وقول الفراء والزمخشري يجعل الاستثناء كلا استثناء

ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r9.claim: He also rejects the weak claim that lā is prohibitive and the alif remains only to maintain the rhyme.
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r9.anchor: وكذلك القول بأن لا في { فلا تنسى } للنهي

ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r10.claim: God promises to teach the Prophet the recitation; he will forget only by God's will through abrogation, a lapse establishing Sunnah, or a lapse followed by reminder.
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r10.anchor: والمعنى أنه تعالى أخبر أنه سيقرئه ،   وأنه لا ينسى إلا ما شاء الله

ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r11.claim: The Prophet is protected from forgetting what he is commanded to convey; any lapse occurs only in one of the stated ways.
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r11.anchor: وهو صلى الله عليه وسلم معصوم من النسيان فيما أمر بتبليغه

ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r12.claim: The promise of recitation follows the command to glorify God: glorification entails reciting revealed Qurʾān, and the Prophet feared forgetting it, so God reassures him.
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r12.anchor: ومناسبة { سنقرئك } لما قبله : أنه لما أمره

ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r13.claim: God knows the Prophet's aloud recitation and his inward fear that the revelation might slip away; His knowledge encompasses all things.
ABUHAYYAN:87:7/r13.anchor: { إنه يعلم الجهر } : أي جهرك بالقرآن ،   { وما يخفى } : أي في نفسك من خوف التفلت

ALUSI:87:7/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:7/r1.claim: The exception is unrestricted from all objects: the Prophet will forget nothing of what God teaches him except what God wills him to forget.
ALUSI:87:7/r1.anchor: استثناء مفرغ من أعم المفاعيل أي لا تنسى أصلاً مما سنقرئكه شيئاً

ALUSI:87:7/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما
ALUSI:87:7/r2.claim: They take the exception as applying forever, and connect what is forgotten with what God decrees abrogated in ruling and recitation.
ALUSI:87:7/r2.anchor: قيل أي أبداً قال الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما وهذا مما قضى الله تعالى نسخة وأن يرتفع حكمه

ALUSI:87:7/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r3.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI:87:7/r3.claim: Al-Kashshāf treats forgetting as a metonym for lifting a text's ruling and recitation: what is abrogated is left and forgotten; the clause thus covers non-forgetting and divinely willed abrogation.
ALUSI:87:7/r3.anchor: في الكشاف أي إلا ما شاء الله فذهب به عن حفظك برفع حكمه وتلاوته وجعل النسيان

ALUSI:87:7/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:7/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī sees no need to make forgetting mean lifting a ruling and recitation; the apparent sense is literal forgetting.
ALUSI:87:7/r4.anchor: وأنا لا أرى ضرورة إلى اعتبار ذلك والباء في برفع الخ للسببية

ALUSI:87:7/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:7/r5.claim: The bāʾ is causal: abrogating recitation and ruling either ordinarily leads to abandoning recitation and no longer recalling the text, or makes forgetting conceivable without objection.
ALUSI:87:7/r5.anchor: والباء في برفع الخ للسببية والمراد إما بيان السبب العادي البعيد

ALUSI:87:7/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:7/r6.claim: There is no need to interpret do not forget as do not cease reciting or acting upon any part of the Qurʾān.
ALUSI:87:7/r6.anchor: فلا حاجة إلى جعل معنى فلا تنسى فلا تترك تلاوة شيء منه والعمل به

ALUSI:87:7/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r7.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI:87:7/r7.claim: The Ṣaḥīḥayn report from ʿĀʾishah that ten known sucklings were among what was revealed, then abrogated by five; this shows abrogation need not mean the Prophet forgot every such text after conveying it.
ALUSI:87:7/r7.anchor: أخرج الشيخان عن عائشة رضي الله عنها كان فيما أنزل عشر رضعات معلومات

ALUSI:87:7/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:7/r8.claim: Some abrogated passages remained preserved by scholars; it is far-fetched, though possible, that the Prophet forgot all of them after conveying them and only some hearers retained them.
ALUSI:87:7/r8.anchor: فإن من ذلك ما يحفظه العلماء إلى اليوم فقد أخرج الشيخان

ALUSI:87:7/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:87:7/r9.claim: One explanation says the Prophet hurried during Gabriel's recitation, so he was told to wait for repeated recitation until he memorized it, with possible later forgetting and recollection.
ALUSI:87:7/r9.anchor: وقيل كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يعجل بالقراءة إذا لقنه جبريل عليه السلام

ALUSI:87:7/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:7/r10.claim: Although remembering after forgetting is obligatory, this passage does not itself establish that the Prophet would remember what he had forgotten.
ALUSI:87:7/r10.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن الذكر بعد النسيان وان كان واجباً إلا أن العلم به لا يستفاد

ALUSI:87:7/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:87:7/r11.claim: Another view takes the exception as a small amount, an idiom that means nearly nothing is forgotten because the unknown exception is less than what remains.
ALUSI:87:7/r11.anchor: لأن المشيئة مجهولة وهو لا محالة أقل من الباقي بعد الاستثناء

ALUSI:87:7/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r12.speaker: صحيح البخاري وغيره
ALUSI:87:7/r12.claim: A report in al-Bukhārī and others says the Prophet omitted a verse during dawn prayer; when Ubay wondered whether it was abrogated, the Prophet said he had forgotten it.
ALUSI:87:7/r12.anchor: وقد جاء في صحيح البخاري وغيره أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أسقط آية في قراءته

ALUSI:87:7/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:87:7/r13.claim: Al-Baḥr reports that, on hearing ʿAbbād ibn Bishr recite, the Prophet said the recitation had reminded him of verses in a certain sūrah.
ALUSI:87:7/r13.anchor: ففي البحر أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال حين سمع قراءة عباد بن بشير

ALUSI:87:7/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:7/r14.claim: The Prophet is not left in even a small, uncorrected lapse: God reminds him or enables someone else to remind him.
ALUSI:87:7/r14.anchor: ثم أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لا يقر على نسيانه القليل أيضاً بل يذكره الله تعالى

ALUSI:87:7/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r15.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:87:7/r15.claim: A further view treats except a little as figurative total negation, like saying there is no fault except that their swords are not sharp.
ALUSI:87:7/r15.anchor: وقيل الاستثناء بمعنى القلة وأريد بها النفي مجازاً كما في قولهم قل من يقول

ALUSI:87:7/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r16.speaker: العصامية
ALUSI:87:7/r16.claim: Al-ʿIṣāmī's gloss on Anwār al-Tanzīl says this exception reinforces universal negation rather than restricting it.
ALUSI:87:7/r16.anchor: وفي الحواشي العصامية على أنوار التنزيل أن الاستثناء على هذا الوجه لتأكيد عموم النفي

ALUSI:87:7/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r17.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI:87:7/r17.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads the exception temporally: the Prophet never forgets except at a time God wills, while God does not in fact will that; the exception displays divine power.
ALUSI:87:7/r17.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب الفراء فقال إنه تعالى ما شاء الله ينسى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم شيئاً

ALUSI:87:7/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:7/r18.claim: The exception teaches that the Prophet's retention is God's favor, not his own power; evidence elsewhere establishes that God does not will actual forgetting, including 75:16.
ALUSI:87:7/r18.anchor: فائدة هذا الاستثناء إن يعرفه الله تعالى قدرته حتى يعلم صلى الله عليه وسلم أن عدم النسيان

ALUSI:87:7/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r19.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:87:7/r19.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Farrāʾ's explanation and the related temporal reading as unsuitable to divine or eloquent speech.
ALUSI:87:7/r19.anchor: وقد أشار أبو حيان إلى ما قاله الفراء وإلى الوجه الذي قبله وإباهما غاية الآباء

ALUSI:87:7/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:7/r20.claim: Al-Ālūsī calls Abū Ḥayyān's rejection rash, saying he failed to grasp the basis of those readings.
ALUSI:87:7/r20.anchor: وإباهما غاية الآباء لعدم الوقوف على حقيقتهما وقال لا ينبغي أن يكون ذلك

ALUSI:87:7/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:7/r21.claim: The assurance concerns complete, lasting forgetfulness that the Prophet would not be corrected for; forgetfulness about foundational religious duties is not left uncorrected.
ALUSI:87:7/r21.anchor: من نفى نسيان شيء من القرآن نفى النسيان التام المستمر مما لا يقر عليه

ALUSI:87:7/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r22.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI:87:7/r22.claim: Al-Rāzī is cited for the view that the Prophet is not left forgetful about core principles and obligations, though he may be concerning other matters or etiquette and sunnahs.
ALUSI:87:7/r22.anchor: ونقل هذا عن الإمام الرازي عليه الرحمة فليحفظ

ALUSI:87:7/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:7/r23.claim: The shift to the majestic name Allah heightens awe and signals that this will belongs to divinity encompassing all attributes.
ALUSI:87:7/r23.anchor: والالتفات إلى الاسم الجليل على سائر الأوجه لتربية المهابة والإيذان بدوران المشيئة

ALUSI:87:7/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r24.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:87:7/r24.claim: Abū Ḥayyān links the reassurance to the command to glorify God: Qurʾānic recitation completes glorification, and God allays the Prophet's fear of forgetting revelation.
ALUSI:87:7/r24.anchor: وقال أبو حيان إنه سبحانه لما أمره صلى الله عليه وسلم بالتسبيح وكان لا يتم

ALUSI:87:7/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:7/r25.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds Abū Ḥayyān's proposed link unconvincing; he favors reading We shall have you recite as explaining glorification or its command, showing the recitation's importance.
ALUSI:87:7/r25.anchor: وفيه نظر لا يخفى ولو قيل إن { سنقرئك } استئناف واقع موقع التعليل

ALUSI:87:7/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r26.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:7/r26.claim: Alternatively, We shall have you recite prepares the Prophet to receive divine effusion through glorification; this points to glorification's merit, supported by reports cited by al-Thaʿlabī and Ibn al-Shaykh.
ALUSI:87:7/r26.anchor: ونحوه كونه في موقع التعليل على معنى هيىء نفسك للإفاضة عليك بتسبيح الله تعالى

ALUSI:87:7/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r27.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:7/r27.claim: The overt and hidden cover what appears in speech, action, and other ways, not speech alone; God knows the Prophet's concern and chooses what to preserve or let him forget according to wisdom.
ALUSI:87:7/r27.anchor: والجهر هنا ما ظهر قولاً أو فعلاً أو غيرهما وليس خاصاً بالأقوال

ALUSI:87:7/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r28.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:87:7/r28.claim: One view takes this clause as emphasis for everything preceding and what follows.
ALUSI:87:7/r28.anchor: وقيل توكيد لجميع ما تقدمه وتوكيد لما بعده

ALUSI:87:7/r29.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:7/r29.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:87:7/r29.claim: Another view makes it emphasize We shall have you recite: God knows the Prophet's audible reading with Gabriel and his fear of forgetting, so he need not worry about what God chooses to retain or abrogate.
ALUSI:87:7/r29.anchor: وقيل توكيد لقوله تعالى : { سَنُقْرِئُكَ } الخ على أن الجهر

BAGHAWI:87:7/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:7/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:87:7/r1.claim: The exception allows God to make the Prophet forget, including Quran whose recitation God abrogates; forgetting is one kind of abrogation.
BAGHAWI:87:7/r1.anchor: { إلا ما شاء الله } أن تنساه ، وما نسخ الله تلاوته من القرآن ، كما قال : { ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها }

BAGHAWI:87:7/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:7/r2.speaker: مجاهد والكلبي
BAGHAWI:87:7/r2.claim: Mujahid and al-Kalbi say the Prophet began reciting each verse before Gabriel had finished it, fearing he would forget; thereafter he forgot nothing.
BAGHAWI:87:7/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد ، والكلبي : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نزل عليه جبريل عليه السلام

BAGHAWI:87:7/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:7/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:87:7/r3.claim: God knows what is overt or hidden in speech and action, meaning the secret and the public.
BAGHAWI:87:7/r3.anchor: { إنه يعلم الجهر } من القول والفعل ، { وما يخفى } منهما ، والمعنى : أنه يعلم السر والعلانية

BAGHAWI:87:8/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:8/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:87:8/r4.claim: Another view connects this promise to the preceding verse: God knows the Prophet's audible recitation to Gabriel and his private rehearsal from fear of forgetting, then eases revelation so he can retain and teach it.
BAGHAWI:87:8/r4.anchor: وقيل : هو متصل بالكلام الأول معناه : أنه يعلم الجهر مما تقرؤه على جبريل إذا فرغ من التلاوة

BAYDAWI:87:7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:7/r1.claim: The exception can mean that God makes the Prophet forget a portion by abrogating its recitation.
BAYDAWI:87:7/r1.anchor: إلا ما شاء الله نسيانه بأن نسخ تلاوته

BAYDAWI:87:7/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:7/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI:87:7/r2.claim: An account says the Prophet omitted a verse in prayer; Ubayy thought it had been abrogated, asked him, and he said he had forgotten it.
BAYDAWI:87:7/r2.anchor: لما روي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أسقط آية في قراءته في الصلاة فحسب أبي أنها نسخت فسأله فقال نسيتها

BAYDAWI:87:7/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:7/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:7/r3.claim: Alternatively, the exception indicates a very small amount, since rarity can be used to mean negation of forgetting altogether.
BAYDAWI:87:7/r3.anchor: أو نفي النسيان رأسا فإن القلة تستعمل للنفي

BAYDAWI:87:7/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:7/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:7/r4.claim: The known outward and hidden matters may be people's conditions, or the Prophet's aloud recitation with Gabriel and his fear of forgetting; God knows what is beneficial to preserve or cause to be forgotten.
BAYDAWI:87:7/r4.anchor: إنه يعلم الجهر وما يخفى ما ظهر من أحوالكم وما بطن أو جهرك بالقراءة مع جبريل

BIQAI:87:7/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:7/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:7/r1.claim: God may will the Prophet to forget a passage because He has abrogated it, abrogating parts of the law according to benefits and easing the community's burden.
BIQAI:87:7/r1.anchor: ينسخ من الشريعة ما يشاء بحسب المصالح

BIQAI:87:7/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:7/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:7/r2.claim: Alternatively, God may make the greatest of creation forget a verse or word, displaying the Qur'an's majesty, then cause him to remember it again.
BIQAI:87:7/r2.anchor: أو لتظهر عظمته في أن أعظم الخلق يغلبه القرآن لأنه صفة الله فتنسى الآية أو الكلمة ثم تذكرها تارة

BIQAI:87:7/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:7/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:7/r3.claim: The Prophet may remember what he forgot either when one of his community reminds him or through another means.
BIQAI:87:7/r3.anchor: فتنسى الآية أو الكلمة ثم تذكرها تارة بتذكير أحد من آحاد أمتك وتارة بغير ذلك

BIQAI:87:7/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:7/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:7/r4.claim: The shift to third person invokes the divine name, whose majesty is greater than explicit wording with an instrument of greatness.
BIQAI:87:7/r4.anchor: قال لافتاً القول إلى سياق الغيبة إعلاماً بأن

BIQAI:87:7/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:7/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:7/r5.claim: The agent who recites and determines what may be forgotten must have encompassing knowledge; whatever God wills comes to pass, as 16:40 says.
BIQAI:87:7/r5.anchor: لا سيما الإقراء والحكم على ما يقرأ

BIQAI:87:7/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:7/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:7/r6.claim: The pronoun in innahu signals God's exalted majesty, beyond creatures' hopes of comprehending Him amid His many acts.

BIQAI:87:7/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:7/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:7/r7.claim: God knows aloud recitation and what is concealed, including private repetition in the Prophet's heart; both are equally known to Him.
BIQAI:87:7/r7.anchor: نسبة الجلي والخفي من جهره بالقرآن وترديده على قلبه سراً وغير ذلك إليه على حد سواء

BIQAI:87:7/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:7/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:7/r8.claim: The overt is named first because it is the discourse's focus; naming it does not restrict God's knowledge, and His knowledge of the hidden entails knowledge of it if disclosed.
BIQAI:87:7/r8.anchor: وأن نسبة الجلي والخفي من جهره بالقرآن

DURR:87:7/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:7/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:87:7/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet began repeating Gabriel’s recitation from fear of forgetting; Gabriel told him no earlier prophet escaped forgetting or having some revelation lifted, and Moses lost four of thirteen scrolls when his emerald tablets broke.
DURR:87:7/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : «كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتاه جبريل بالوحي

DURR:87:7/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:7/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:87:7/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the exception as meaning: unless God wills to make the Prophet forget.
DURR:87:7/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس { سنقرئك فلا تنسى إلا ما شاء الله } يقول إلا ما شئت أنا فأنسيك .

DURR:87:7/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:7/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR:87:7/r6.claim: Qatada says the Messenger did not forget anything except what God willed; he glosses what is hidden as inward whispering.
DURR:87:7/r6.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { سنقرئك فلا تنسى إلا ما شاء الله } قال : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا ينسى شيئاً

DURR:87:7/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:7/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:87:7/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr explains what is hidden as what a person conceals within himself.
DURR:87:7/r7.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة وابن أبي حاتم عن سعيد بن جبير { إنه يعلم الجهر وما يخفى } قال : ما أخفيت في نفسك .

IBNASHUR:87:7/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:7/r1.claim: The exception branches from “you forget”; mā is a relative pronoun, with “that God wills you to forget” understood.
IBNASHUR:87:7/r1.anchor: والاستثناء في قوله :  { إلا ما شاء الله }

IBNASHUR:87:7/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:7/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:7/r2.claim: The exception means that the Prophet may forget some revealed Quran if God wills it; Ibn ʿĀshūr distinguishes two kinds.
IBNASHUR:87:7/r2.anchor: أن بعض القرآن ينساه النبي إذا شاء الله أن ينساه

IBNASHUR:87:7/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:7/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:7/r3.claim: The more apparent kind is divinely ordered abrogation of recitation: the Prophet and Muslims cease reciting the passage until they forget it.
IBNASHUR:87:7/r3.anchor: وهو أظهرهما أن الله إذا شاء نسخ تلاوة بعض ما أنزل

IBNASHUR:87:7/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:7/r4.speaker: عمر
IBNASHUR:87:7/r4.claim: ʿUmar reported that the stoning passage and a warning against disavowing one’s fathers had once been revealed and recited.
IBNASHUR:87:7/r4.anchor: ما روي عن عمر أنه قال :  « كان فيما أنزل الشيخُ والشيخه

IBNASHUR:87:7/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:7/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:7/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr connects this abrogation of recitation with the reading “or cause it to be forgotten” in al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR:87:7/r5.anchor: وهذا ما أشير إليه بقوله تعالى :  { أو ننسها }

IBNASHUR:87:7/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:7/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:7/r6.claim: The other kind is temporary human lapse in the Prophet’s memory, after which God provides a reminder.
IBNASHUR:87:7/r6.anchor: ما يعرض نسيانه للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم نسياناً موقتاً كشأن عوارض

IBNASHUR:87:7/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:7/r7.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR:87:7/r7.claim: In a report in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, ʿĀʾisha says a nighttime recitation by a man reminded the Prophet of verses he had omitted or forgotten.
IBNASHUR:87:7/r7.anchor: ففي « صحيح البخاري » عن عائشة قالت :  « سمع النبيءُ صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلاً

IBNASHUR:87:7/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:7/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR:87:7/r8.claim: Another Bukhārī report says Ubayy ibn Kaʿb asked whether a verse omitted in prayer had been abrogated; the Prophet replied, “I forgot it.”
IBNASHUR:87:7/r8.anchor: وفيه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أسقط آية في قراءته في الصلاة فسأله أبي بن كعب

IBNASHUR:87:7/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:7/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:7/r9.claim: “You will not forget” is not a prohibition, since involuntary forgetting is outside legal duty; treating lā as prohibitive strains the explanation of its written alif.
IBNASHUR:87:7/r9.anchor: وليس قوله :  { فلا تنسى } من الخبر المستعمل في النهي عن النسيان

IBNASHUR:87:7/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:7/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:7/r10.claim: The clause about God knowing what is manifest and hidden is parenthetical and explains the promise that the Quran will be preserved from accidental loss.
IBNASHUR:87:7/r10.anchor: وجملة :  { إنه يعلم الجهر وما يخفى } معترضة وهي تعليل

IBNASHUR:87:7/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:7/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:7/r11.claim: The Prophet’s spoken recitation is manifest to God, while a forgotten verse is hidden in memory and fails to emerge in speech, yet God knows it.
IBNASHUR:87:7/r11.anchor: ومناسبة الجهر وما يخفى أن ما يقرؤه الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم من القرآن هو من قبيل الجهر

IBNATIYYA:87:7/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and others take the exception as what God decreed to abrogate, removing both its recitation and ruling.
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r1.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة وغيره مما قضى الله تعالى بنسخه ، وأن ترفع تلاوته وحكمه

IBNATIYYA:87:7/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and other scholars of meaning treat the exception as a conventional connective expression; nothing is thereby permitted to be forgotten.
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء وجماعة من أهل المعاني : هو استثناء صلة في الكلام على سنة الله تعالى في الاستثناء ، وليس ثم شيء أبيح نسيانه

IBNATIYYA:87:7/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God may cause the Prophet to forget something so that he can establish a practice, as the Prophet said he forgets or is made to forget for that purpose.
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : { إلا ما شاء الله } أن ينسيكه لتسن به على نحو قوله عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA:87:7/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r4.speaker: بعض المتأولين
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r4.claim: Some interpreters say God may let the Prophet forget something temporarily and then remind him of it.
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r4.anchor: وقال بعض المتأولين : { إلا ما شاء الله } أن يغلبك النسيان عليه ثم يذكرك به بعد

IBNATIYYA:87:7/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r5.claim: After hearing ʿAbbād ibn Bishr recite, the Prophet said the recitation reminded him of verses he had omitted from a sūra.
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r5.anchor: ومن هذا قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين سمع قراءة عباد بن بشر يرحمه الله : «لقد أذكرني كذا في سورة كذا وكذا

IBNATIYYA:87:7/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r6.claim: The Prophet cannot forget what he was commanded to convey; after conveying and retaining it, he may forget and later recall it, establish a practice, or undergo abrogation.
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r6.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد : ونسيان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ممتنع فيما أمر بتبليغه ، إذ هو معصوم فإذا بلغه ووعي عنه ، فالنسيان جائز على أن يتذكر بعد ذلك وعلى أن يسنَّ ، أو على النسخ

IBNATIYYA:87:7/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r7.claim: God encompasses all things in knowledge, knowing what is manifest and hidden; this assures that He reminds the Prophet of anything forgotten.
IBNATIYYA:87:7/r7.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى { إنه يعلم الجهر } من الأشياء { وما يخفى } منها ، وذلك لإحاطته بكل شيء علماً

IBNKATHIR:87:7/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:7/r1.claim: God tells and promises Muhammad that He will recite to him so he does not forget, except what God wills.
IBNKATHIR:87:7/r1.anchor: وهذا إخبار من الله ، عز وجل ، ووعد منه له ، بأنه سيقرئه قراءة لا ينساها ، { إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ }

IBNKATHIR:87:7/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:7/r2.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR:87:7/r2.claim: Ibn Jarir chooses the promise that Muhammad will not forget what God recites, except what God wills.
IBNKATHIR:87:7/r2.anchor: قراءة لا ينساها ، { إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ } وهذا اختيار ابن جرير

IBNKATHIR:87:7/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:7/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR:87:7/r3.claim: Qatada says the Messenger of God did not forget anything except what God willed.
IBNKATHIR:87:7/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا ينسى شيئا إلا ما شاء الله

IBNKATHIR:87:7/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:7/r4.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR:87:7/r4.claim: An alternative takes “do not forget” as a command, with the exception referring to what God abrogates, which Muhammad may leave aside without blame.
IBNKATHIR:87:7/r4.anchor: وقيل : المراد بقوله : { فَلا تَنْسَى } طلب ، وجعلوا معنى الاستثناء على هذا ما يقع من النسخ

IBNKATHIR:87:7/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:7/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:7/r5.claim: God knows what people say and do openly or secretly; nothing of it is hidden from Him.
IBNKATHIR:87:7/r5.anchor: أي : يعلم ما يجهر به العباد وما يخفونه من أقوالهم وأفعالهم ، لا يخفى عليه من ذلك شيء

MAWARDI:87:7/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:7/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
MAWARDI:87:7/r1.claim: The exception means whatever God wills to abrogate, so the Prophet forgets it.
MAWARDI:87:7/r1.anchor: إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسخه فتنساه ، قاله الحسن وقتادة

MAWARDI:87:7/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:7/r2.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI:87:7/r2.claim: The exception means whatever God wills to delay in sending down, so the Prophet has not yet recited it.
MAWARDI:87:7/r2.anchor: إلا ما شاء الله أن يؤخر إنزاله عليك فلا تقرؤه ، حكاه ابن عيسى

MAWARDI:87:7/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:7/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:87:7/r3.claim: One reading takes what is manifest as the Qurʾān retained in the Prophet’s heart and what is hidden as what was erased from his memory.
MAWARDI:87:7/r3.anchor: أن الجهر ما حفظته من القرآن في صدرك ، وما يخفى هو ما نسخ

MAWARDI:87:7/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:7/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:87:7/r4.claim: What is manifest is what one knows, while what is hidden is what one will put into practice later.
MAWARDI:87:7/r4.anchor: أن الجهر ما علمه ، وما يخفى ما يستعمله من بعد ، قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI:87:7/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:7/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI:87:7/r5.claim: Another reading takes the manifest as what a person has made apparent and the hidden as the acts of obedience they have left undone.
MAWARDI:87:7/r5.anchor: أن الجهر ما قد أظهره ، وما يخفى ما تركه من الطاعات

NASAFI:87:7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:7/r1.claim: The exception is what God wills to abrogate; this reassures the Prophet that revelation is preserved except where God removes both ruling and recitation.
NASAFI:87:7/r1.anchor: { إِلاَّ مَا شَاء الله } أن ينسخه وهذا بشارة من الله لنبيه

NASAFI:87:7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:7/r2.speaker: ابن كيسان النحوي
NASAFI:87:7/r2.claim: Ibn Kaysan asked Junayd about the exception; the exchange explains it as not forgetting to act on the revelation.
NASAFI:87:7/r2.anchor: وسأل ابن كيسان النحوي جنيداً عنه فقال : فلا ننسى العمل به

NASAFI:87:7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:7/r3.speaker: جنيد
NASAFI:87:7/r3.claim: Junayd replied to Ibn Kaysan, “Someone like you is asked for a ruling.”

NASAFI:87:7/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:7/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:7/r4.claim: An alternative takes “do not forget” as a prohibition, with an extra alif for the verse ending, as in 33:67.
NASAFI:87:7/r4.anchor: وقيل : قوله { فَلاَ تنسى } على النهي والألف مزيدة للفاصلة كقوله : { السبيلا }

NASAFI:87:7/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:7/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:7/r5.claim: On the prohibitive reading, the exception is what God causes the Prophet to forget by removing its recitation.
NASAFI:87:7/r5.anchor: إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسيكه برفع تلاوته

NASAFI:87:7/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:7/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:7/r6.claim: God knows the Prophet's audible reading alongside Gabriel, prompted by fear the revelation might slip away, and the thoughts that prompt him to read aloud.
NASAFI:87:7/r6.anchor: إنك تجهر بالقراءة مع قراءة جبريل مخافة التفلت والله يعلم جهرك معه

NASAFI:87:7/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:7/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:7/r7.claim: Alternatively, God knows what the Prophet recites silently because he fears forgetting.
NASAFI:87:7/r7.anchor: أو ما تقرأ في نفسك مخافة النسيان

NASAFI:87:7/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:7/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:7/r8.claim: Alternatively, God knows people's secret and public words and deeds and their outward and inward states.
NASAFI:87:7/r8.anchor: أو يعلم ما أسررتم وما أعلنتم من أقوالكم وأفعالكم

QURTUBI:87:7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:7/r1.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:87:7/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes the exception to mean that God will not will the Prophet to forget anything, comparing the construction with the exception in Hūd 11:108.
QURTUBI:87:7/r1.anchor: ما قاله الفراء : إلا ما شاء الله ، وهو لم يشأ أن تنسى شيئا

QURTUBI:87:7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:7/r2.claim: The idiom I will give you everything you ask except what you wish can express an intention to withhold nothing.
QURTUBI:87:7/r2.anchor: ويقال في الكلام : لأعطينك كل ما سألت إلا ما شئت

QURTUBI:87:7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:7/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:7/r3.claim: On this construction, oath exceptions follow the swearer's intention of completing the oath rather than withholding anything.
QURTUBI:87:7/r3.anchor: فعلى هذا مجاري الإيمان ، يستثنى فيها ونية الحالف التمام

QURTUBI:87:7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:7/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:87:7/r4.claim: Through Abū Ṣāliḥ, Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet did not forget anything after this verse was revealed until he died.
QURTUBI:87:7/r4.anchor: وفي رواية أبي صالح عن ابن عباس : فلم ينس بعد نزول هذه الآية حتى مات

QURTUBI:87:7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:7/r5.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI:87:7/r5.claim: Saʿīd reports Qatāda's statement that the Messenger of God forgot nothing, except as the verse qualifies.
QURTUBI:87:7/r5.anchor: وعن سعيد عن قتادة ، قال : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا ينسى شيئا

QURTUBI:87:7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:7/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:7/r6.claim: One explanation allows that God could will the Prophet to forget, while affirming that he forgot none of the revelation after this verse descended.
QURTUBI:87:7/r6.anchor: وعلى هذه الأقوال قيل : إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسى ، ولكنه لم ينسى شيئا منه

QURTUBI:87:7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:7/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:7/r7.claim: Another view allows temporary forgetting followed by recollection, so the Prophet could forget without losing the passage permanently.
QURTUBI:87:7/r7.anchor: وقيل : إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسى ، ثم يذكر بعد ذلك

QURTUBI:87:7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:7/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:7/r8.claim: An unnamed report says the Prophet omitted a verse during prayer; Ubay thought it had been abrogated, but the Prophet said he had forgotten it.
QURTUBI:87:7/r8.anchor: وقد روي أنه أسقط آية في قراءته في الصلاة ، فحسب أبي أنها نسخت

QURTUBI:87:7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:7/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:7/r9.claim: Some understand forgetting as abrogation, distinguishing the abrogation of recitation from leaving practice after its ruling is abrogated.
QURTUBI:87:7/r9.anchor: ثم قيل : هذا بمعنى النسخ ، أي إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسخه . والاستثناء نوع من النسخ

QURTUBI:87:7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:7/r10.speaker: الفرغاني
QURTUBI:87:7/r10.claim: Al-Farghānī recounts that Ibn Kaysān answered Junayd's question by glossing do not forget as do not fail to act on the revelation; Ibn Kaysān praised the answer.
QURTUBI:87:7/r10.anchor: قال الفرغاني : كان يغشى مجلس الجنيد أهل البسط من العلوم ، وكان يغشاه ابن كيسان النحوي

QURTUBI:87:7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:7/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:7/r11.claim: Lā tansā is read as negation rather than prohibition; the prohibition reading takes it as a command not to neglect recitation, with forgetting possible if recitation is removed.

QURTUBI:87:7/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:7/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:7/r12.claim: The author prefers negation: an exception from a prohibition is ordinarily bounded by a known time, and the yāʾ is written in every codex and read by the reciters.
QURTUBI:87:7/r12.anchor: والأول هو المختار ؛ لأن الاستثناء من النهي لا يكاد يكون إلا مؤقتا معلوما

QURTUBI:87:7/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:7/r13.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:7/r13.claim: Another explanation reads the exception as God's willing to delay the revelation's descent.
QURTUBI:87:7/r13.anchor: وقيل : معناه إلا ما شاء الله أن يؤخر إنزاله

QURTUBI:87:7/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:7/r14.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:7/r14.claim: A further view connects the exception to the pasture becoming dry debris: what people and animals benefit from is spared that fate.
QURTUBI:87:7/r14.anchor: وقيل : المعنى فجعله غثاء أحوى إلا ما شاء الله أن ينال بنو آدم

QURTUBI:87:7/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:7/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:7/r15.claim: Al-jahr is what is expressed openly in speech and deeds, while what is hidden is secret.
QURTUBI:87:7/r15.anchor: أي الإعلان من القول والعمل . " وما يخفى " من السر

QURTUBI:87:7/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:7/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:87:7/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains what is hidden as what lies in one's heart and self.
QURTUBI:87:7/r16.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : ما في قلبك ونفسك

QURTUBI:87:7/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:7/r17.speaker: محمد بن حاتم
QURTUBI:87:7/r17.claim: Muḥammad ibn Ḥātim takes the contrast as publicizing charity versus concealing it.
QURTUBI:87:7/r17.anchor: وقال محمد بن حاتم : يعلم إعلان الصدقة وإخفاءها

QURTUBI:87:7/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:7/r18.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:7/r18.claim: Another view makes what is public the Quran memorized in the Prophet's chest and what is hidden the recitation abrogated from it.
QURTUBI:87:7/r18.anchor: وقيل : الجهر ما حفظته من القرآن في صدرك

TAB:87:7/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:7/r1.speaker: author
TAB:87:7/r1.claim: God will make Muhammad recite the Qurʾān without forgetting, except what God wills.
TAB:87:7/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره :  سنقرئك يا محمد هذا القرآن فلا تنساه

TAB:87:7/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:7/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TAB:87:7/r2.claim: One view takes this as God's assurance that He will teach and preserve the Qurʾān for Muhammad, while telling him not to rush its recitation, as in 75:16–17.
TAB:87:7/r2.anchor: فقال بعضهم :  هذا إخبار من الله نبيه عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه يعلمه هذا القرآن

TAB:87:7/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:7/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:87:7/r3.claim: Mujahid reports that Muhammad used to rehearse the Qurʾān inwardly for fear of forgetting it.
TAB:87:7/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   قوله :  سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلا تَنْسَى

TAB:87:7/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:7/r4.speaker: قائلو هذه المقالة
TAB:87:7/r4.claim: Those holding the first view understand the exception as what God wills Muhammad to forget: material whose recitation and ruling God abrogated.
TAB:87:7/r4.anchor: قائلو هذه المقالة :  معنى الاستثناء في هذا الموضع على النسيان

TAB:87:7/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:7/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB:87:7/r5.claim: Another view reads nisyān as abandoning practice: Muhammad will not leave any Qurʾānic teaching except what God wills him to stop practicing through abrogation.
TAB:87:7/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون :  معنى النسيان في هذا الموضع :  الترك

TAB:87:7/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:7/r6.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB:87:7/r6.claim: A grammarian says God did not will Muhammad to forget anything; the exception is conventional wording with no intended exception, as in oaths.
TAB:87:7/r6.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية يقول في ذلك :  لم يشأ الله أن تنسى شيئا

TAB:87:7/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:7/r7.speaker: author
TAB:87:7/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that Muhammad forget only what God wills him to forget by abrogating and removing it, as the clearest meaning.
TAB:87:7/r7.anchor: قول من قال :  معنى ذلك :  فلا تنسى إلاّ أن نشاء نحن أن نُنسيكه

TAB:87:7/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:7/r8.speaker: author
TAB:87:7/r8.claim: God knows all Muhammad's deeds, public and hidden, so he must beware of acting against God's command in any circumstance.
TAB:87:7/r8.anchor: وأنت عامل في حال من أحوالك

DURR:87:6/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:87:6/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās recounts the Prophet’s fear of forgetting revelation, Gabriel’s reassurance, the promise of preservation except what God willed, forgotten or lifted non-legal verses, and Moses’ broken tablets.
DURR:87:6/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : «كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتاه جبريل بالوحي لم يفرغ جبريل من الوحي

DURR:87:6/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:6/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:87:6/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains “except what God wills” as God’s choosing to make the Prophet forget something.
DURR:87:6/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس { سنقرئك فلا تنسى إلا ما شاء الله } يقول إلا ما شئت أنا فأنسيك .

DURR:87:6/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:6/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR:87:6/r6.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet forgot nothing except what God willed; public and hidden knowledge includes inner whispering.
DURR:87:6/r6.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { سنقرئك فلا تنسى إلا ما شاء الله } قال : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا ينسى شيئا إلا ما شاء الله

IBNKATHIR:87:6/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:6/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:6/r5.claim: God knows whatever people say or do openly or secretly; nothing is hidden from Him.
IBNKATHIR:87:6/r5.anchor: أي : يعلم ما يجهر به العباد وما يخفونه من أقوالهم وأفعالهم ، لا يخفى عليه من ذلك شيء

QASHANI:87:6-10/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:6-10/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:6-10/r3.claim: God knows the perfection already manifest in the Prophet and the perfection still latent in him.
QASHANI:87:6-10/r3.anchor: أي: ما ظهر فيك من الكمال

NAHHAS:v5p205/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p205/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p205/r5.claim: The exception is accusative as an exception.

NAHHAS:v5p205/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p205/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p205/r6.claim: If verse 6 means 'do not leave,' the exception concerns an order God abrogates and then commands the Prophet to leave.
NAHHAS:v5p205/r6.anchor: إلا ما شاء الله جل وعز أن ننسخه فيأمرك بتركه

NAHHAS:v5p205/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p205/r7.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p205/r7.claim: One reading allows forgetting only what God wills but says He will not will him to forget it; al-Farra compares 11:107.
NAHHAS:v5p205/r7.anchor: ولا يشاء الله أن تنسى منه شيئا وهذا قول الفراء

NAHHAS:v5p205/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p205/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p205/r8.claim: Another reading allows ordinary lapses that affect human beings.
NAHHAS:v5p205/r8.anchor: إلا ما شاء الله مما يلحق الآدميين

NAHHAS:v5p205/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p205/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p205/r9.claim: A further reading refers to God removing a verse and its recitation.
NAHHAS:v5p205/r9.anchor: ما شاء الله أن يرفعه ويرفع تلاوته

NAHHAS:v5p205/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p205/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p205/r10.claim: A fifth syntactic possibility attaches the exception to the description of pasture as withered debris.
NAHHAS:v5p205/r10.anchor: فجعله غثاء أحوى إلا ما شاء الله

NAHHAS:v5p205/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p205/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p205/r11.claim: God knows what is manifest and concealed, so people should avoid sins both public and private.
