NAHHAS:v5p205/r11.anchor: أي ما ظهر وعلن ( وما يخفى ) ما كتم

ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r3.claim: One interpretation allows the Prophet to forget something temporarily and then remember it.
ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r3.anchor: فقيل إلا ما شاء الله ثم يذكره بعد

ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that God may defer some Quranic revelation.
ZAJJAJ:v5p315#2/r4.anchor: وقيل إلا ما شاء الله أن يؤخره من القرآن

ASAD-NOTES:87:6/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:6/r3.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:6/r3.claim: God knows what is perceptible to human beings and what is hidden from them.
ASAD-NOTES:87:6/r3.anchor: knows all that is open to [man's] perception as well as all that is hidden [from it]

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1-8:kommentar/r9.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1-8:kommentar/r9.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1-8:kommentar/r9.claim: Verse 7 appears to be a later insertion harmonizing verse 6's promise not to forget with 2:106's allowance that God may make Muhammad forget verses.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1-8:kommentar/r9.anchor: Die nachträgliche Einfügung von V. 7 dient dazu, den zweiten Teil

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.claim: The preceding sūrah urges the Prophet to wait: persistent deniers receive only temporary respite under God's practice, and cannot escape His grasp.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.anchor: Sūrah al-Ṭāriq, the previous sūrah ended on urging the Prophet (sws) to show patience and to wait for the decision of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.claim: This sūrah shifts its primary address from stubborn Quraysh to the Prophet and, over at least ten following sūrahs, dispels his preaching fears in varied ways.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.anchor: while ignoring these stubborn elements from among the Quraysh, the Prophet (sws) is addressed directly and given glad tidings

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r4.claim: Verses 6–8 promise that revelation will mature for the Prophet, remain preserved except for what God wills to set aside, and bring ease from known hardships.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r4.anchor: The favour of revelations that he is receiving will gradually reach its culmination

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r2.claim: God guarantees the Qur'an's preservation so the Prophet will not forget; collection, recital, following, and explanation are all assigned to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r2.anchor: Indeed, upon Us is its collection and recital. So when We have recited it out, follow this recital. Then upon Us is to explain it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r4.claim: God knows the Prophet's circumstances, worries, and prayers as well as his enemies' overt tricks and hidden plots; His knowledge and power ensure needed help.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p277/r4.anchor: all his worries as well as his prayers

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p278/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p278/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p278/r1.claim: True faith and trust arise from firm awareness of God's all-embracing knowledge and all-encompassing power.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p278/r1.anchor: true faith and trust in God

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r2.claim: God knows the Prophet's audible Qur'an recitation and his private fear that it might escape him, and has relieved that fear by promising to recite it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p457/r2.anchor: جهرك بالقرآن، وما يخفى: أي في نفسك من خوف التفلت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p401/r4.claim: God knows what people make public in speech and action and what they conceal; in other words, He knows secret and open matters.

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r7.claim: The known and hidden may mean people's outward and inward states, or the Prophet's public recitation with Gabriel and his private fear; God knows what preservation or forgetting benefits them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r7.anchor: ما ظهر من أحوالكم وما بطن، أو جهرك بالقراءة مع جبريل

DURR-FULL:v8p483/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r3.claim: The exception means except what God chooses to make the Prophet forget.
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس {سنقرئك فلا تنسى إلا ما شاء الله} يقول إلا ما شئت أنا فأنسيك

DURR-FULL:v8p483/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r4.claim: The Prophet forgot nothing except what God willed; what God knows as hidden includes whispered thoughts.
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {سنقرئك فلا تنسى إلا ما شاء الله} قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا ينسى شيئا

DURR-FULL:v8p483/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r5.claim: The hidden matters God knows are what a person conceals within himself.
DURR-FULL:v8p483/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير {إنه يعلم الجهر وما يخفى} قال: ما أخفيت في نفسك

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#4/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#4/r2.claim: The exception means what God wills to make the Prophet forget.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#4/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس سنقرئك فلا تنسى الا ما شاء الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p281/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p281/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p281/r4.claim: The statement that God knows what is manifest and hidden is an interruption explaining His guarantee: public recitation is manifest, while omitted forgotten recitation is hidden.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p281/r4.anchor: ومناسبة الجهر وما يخفى أن ما يقرؤه الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم من القرآن هو من قبيل الجهر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r4.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and others say the exception concerns material whose recitation and legal ruling God abrogates.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r4.anchor: الحسن وقتادة وغيره مما قضى الله تعالى بنسخه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r5.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r5.claim: Al-Farra and other linguists regard the exception as a conventional parenthetical expression, with nothing actually permitted to be forgotten.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء وجماعة من أهل المعاني: هو استثناء صلة في الكلام على سنة الله تعالى في الاستثناء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says God may make the Prophet forget something so he can establish a Sunnah, as in the saying I forget or am made to forget for that purpose.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسيكه لتسن به على نحو قوله عليه السلام: «إني لأنسى أو أنسى لأسن»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r7.claim: Some exegetes say God may let the Prophet forget temporarily and then remind him, as happened when another man's recitation reminded him of verses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r7.anchor: وقال بعض المتأولين: إلا ما شاء الله أن يغلبك النسيان عليه ثم يذكرك به بعد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r8.claim: For what he is commanded to convey, the Prophet is protected from forgetting; after learning it he may forget and later recall it, establish a Sunnah, or experience abrogation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r8.anchor: ونسيان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ممتنع فيما أمر بتبليغه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r9.claim: God's knowledge encompasses manifest and hidden things, validating the report that He reminds the Prophet of what he has forgotten.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p469/r9.anchor: لإحاطته بكل شيء علما، وبهذا يصح الخبر بأنه لا ينسى شيئا إلا ذكره الله تعالى به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379#2/r4.claim: God knows what people say and do openly and secretly; nothing of it is hidden from Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379#2/r4.anchor: أي: يعلم ما يجهر به العباد وما يخفونه من أقوالهم وأفعالهم، لا يخفى عليه من ذلك شيء.

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r3.claim: Jahr is raising the voice, opposite to the quietness of whispering.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r3.anchor: والجهر: رفع الصوت، ونقيضه: الهمس، وهو ضعف الصوت

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r7.claim: One interpretation says what is manifest is the Qur’an retained in the heart and what is hidden is what has been erased from memory.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r7.anchor: أن الجهر ما حفظته من القرآن في صدرك , وما يخفى هو ما نسخ من حفظك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says the manifest is what God already knows and the hidden is what the person will learn later.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r8.anchor: أن الجهر ما علمه , وما يخفى ما سيتعلمه من بعد , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r9.claim: A third view takes the manifest as what has been displayed and the hidden as acts of obedience left undone.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r9.anchor: أن الجهر ما قد أظهره , وما يخفى ما تركه من الطاعات .

MUQATIL:87:1-7/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r7.speaker: مقاتل
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r7.claim: God knows what is spoken or done openly and what is hidden of either.
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r7.anchor: ثم قال: { إنه يعلم الجهر وما يخفى } [آية: 7] يعلم الجهر من القول والفعل

RAZI-FULL:v31p129#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p129#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p129#2/r1.claim: One reading says God knows Muhammad’s audible recitation with Gabriel as well as his hidden fear of forgetting, reassuring him that God will care for the matter.
RAZI-FULL:v31p129#2/r1.anchor: أنه سبحانه عالم بجهرك في القراءة مع قراءة جبريل عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v31p129#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p129#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p129#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, God knows the recited passage and what He abrogates, since He knows what benefits His servants.
RAZI-FULL:v31p129#2/r2.anchor: فلا تنسى إلا ما شاء الله أن ينسخ ، فإنه أعلم بمصالح العبيد

TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r3.claim: Al-jahr is what is fully perceptible to sight or hearing; here it means the manifest, opposed to what is hidden.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r3.anchor: والمراد بالجهر الظاهر للإدراك بقرينة مقابلته لقوله { وما يخفى }

TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r4.claim: God's knowledge of the manifest and hidden explains the guarantee because He knows the Prophet's concern for revelation and obedience.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r4.anchor: والجملة في مقام التعليل لقوله. { سنقرئك فلا تنسى } والمعنى سنصلح لك بالك

TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r5.claim: The shift to third-person ‘He knows’ points to divine power as the basis of the exception.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#3/r5.anchor: التفات من التكلم مع الغير إلى الغيبة والنكتة فيه الإشارة إلى حجة الاستثناء

THALABI:v10p184/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184/r4.speaker: محمد بن حامد
THALABI:v10p184/r4.claim: Muḥammad ibn Ḥāmid glosses the manifest and hidden as openly and secretly giving charity.
THALABI:v10p184/r4.anchor: قال محمد بن حامد: يعلم إعلان الصدقة وإخفاءها

THALABI:v10p184/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p184/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p184/r5.claim: Another explanation says God knows the Prophet's recitation aloud to Gabriel and silent rehearsal.
THALABI:v10p184/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو متصل بالكلام الأول معناه: نعلم الجهر

ELMALILI:87:6/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r9.claim: The exception does not limit God’s power: He can withdraw the granted memory and make the Prophet forget completely, which would amount to abrogation under 2:106.
ELMALILI:87:6/r9.anchor: O’nu hiçbir şey âciz bırakamaz. Böyle kuvvetli bir hâfıza kudreti verdikten sonra O dilerse onu selbeder. Unutturacağını tamamen unutturabilir ki bu bir nesh olur.

ELMALILI:87:6/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r10.claim: Elmalılı cites a report in Sahih al-Bukhari: the Prophet omitted a verse in the dawn prayer; Ubayy thought it had been abrogated, asked him, and the Prophet said he had forgotten.
ELMALILI:87:6/r10.anchor: Übeyy onu neshedildi sanmış, sual etmişti.[^5] Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm “unuttum” buyurmuştu.[^6]

ELMALILI:87:6/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r11.claim: If the Prophet rarely forgot, God did not leave him in that state but reminded him or provided a means of remembrance.
ELMALILI:87:6/r11.anchor: Resûlullah’ta böyle nâdiren nisyan vâki‘olursa Allah teâlâ onu bırakmaz, hatırlatır veya hatırlatacak bir sebep müyesser kılardı.

ELMALILI:87:6/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r12.claim: Elmalılı cites Bahr for the report that hearing Abbād b. Bishr recite reminded the Prophet of a verse in a particular sura.
ELMALILI:87:6/r12.anchor: Abbâd b. Bişr’in[^8] kıraatini işittiğinde “Bu bana filan ve filan sûrede, şu ve şu âyeti hatırlattı” buyurmuştu.

ELMALILI:87:6/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r13.claim: An interpretation takes the exception as allowing only rare forgetfulness, as illustrated by the cited rare lapse in prayer recitation.
ELMALILI:87:6/r13.anchor: Denilmiştir ki istisnâ kıllet içindir. Nitekim Sahîh-i Buhârî’de rivayet edilmiştir

ELMALILI:87:6/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r14.claim: Such momentary lapses are not continuing forgetfulness in the sense of abrogation; they teach rulings about lapses that the community cannot avoid in recitation and prayer.
ELMALILI:87:6/r14.anchor: bir iki an için li-hikmetin vâki‘olan cüz’î nisyan buna münâfî olmaz.

ELMALILI:87:6/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r15.claim: Another analysis places the exception before the promise not to forget.

ELMALILI:87:6/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r16.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:87:6/r16.claim: Some explain the exception as rarity used metaphorically for negation: saying something is rarely said can mean it is not said.
ELMALILI:87:6/r16.anchor: bazıları da demişlerdir ki bu istisnâ kıllet mânasına olarak nefiyden mecazdır

ELMALILI:87:6/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r17.claim: A poetic example shows exception after a negation can intensify praise by mentioning only sword nicks from battle, a rhetorical device called praise through what suggests blame.
ELMALILI:87:6/r17.anchor: وَلاَ عَيْبَ فِيهِم غَيْرَ أنَّ سُيُوفَهُمْ لَهُنَّ فُلُولٌ مِنْ قِرَاعِ الكَتَائِبِ

ELMALILI:87:6/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r18.speaker: İsam
ELMALILI:87:6/r18.claim: As cited by Alusi from the Qadi gloss, the exception emphasizes the universal negation rather than limiting it: the Prophet will never forget, though God could will otherwise; this resembles the exception for the people of Paradise in 11:107–108.
ELMALILI:87:6/r18.anchor: Kāzî hâşiyesinde İsam demiştir ki: “Bu veche göre istisnâ, nefyin umumunu tekid içindir, nakz-ı umum için değildir.

ELMALILI:87:6/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r19.speaker: Ferrâ
ELMALILI:87:6/r19.claim: Ferrā says God did not will to make the Prophet forget; the exception only indicates that God could do so, as in 17:86.
ELMALILI:87:6/r19.anchor: Ferrâ buna zâhib olmuş ve demiştir ki: ‘Bu istisnâ ile Allah teâlâ Peygamberine hiçbir şeyi unutturmayı dilememiş

ELMALILI:87:6/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r20.claim: Like the hypothetical warning about shirk in 39:65, the exception stresses that forgetting will not occur and that the Prophet’s retention is solely God’s favor, not his own power.
ELMALILI:87:6/r20.anchor: burada da bundan sonra nisyânın velev az olsun vukū‘una değil, asla vâki‘olmayacağına ve şu kadar ki onun unutmaması kendi kuvvetinden değil, mahza Allah’ın fazl u ihsânından olduğuna tenbih içindir.

ELMALILI:87:6/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r21.claim: Elmalılı rejects Abu Hayyan’s criticism of Ferrā’s literary interpretation and agrees with Alusi and Abduh that Ferrā’s reading is sound.
ELMALILI:87:6/r21.anchor: Âlûsî gibi Abduh da Ferrâ’nın bu tevcîhini takdirde isabet eylemişlerdir.

ELMALILI:87:6/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r22.claim: On Ferrā’s reading, the promise excludes continuing forgetfulness, not a momentary lapse for a purpose; whether the exception means rarity or emphasis, the continuing non-forgetfulness is a miracle.
ELMALILI:87:6/r22.anchor: nisyandan murad müstemirren nisyandır. Binâen‘aleyh müstakir olmamak üzere haberde vârid olduğu gibi bir iki an için li-hikmetin vâki‘olan cüz’î nisyan buna münâfî olmaz.

ELMALILI:87:6/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:6/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:6/r23.claim: Using the all-comprehensive divine name Allah for the promise and will cultivates awe and shows that the gift rests on the totality of divine names and attributes; “Lord Most High” confirms it.
ELMALILI:87:6/r23.anchor: sâir esmâ ve sıfâtta değil de hepsini câmi‘olan ulûhiyet unvânı üzerine

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r4.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r4.claim: Some exegetes say the exception indicates abrogation: God makes the Prophet forget a ruling when He wants to repeal it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r4.anchor: Bazıları bu istisnanın neshe delâlet ettiğini yani “Allah herhangi bir hükmü yürürlükten kaldırmak istediği zaman onu peygambere unutturur” mânasına geldiğini ifade ederler.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r5.speaker: Bazı âlimler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r5.claim: Other scholars read the exception like 17:86 and 11:107–108: God never willed the Prophet to forget, so he never did.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r5.anchor: Bazı âlimlere göre ise bu âyet –tıpkı “Gerçek şu ki, biz dilersek sana vahyettiğimizi ortadan kaldırırız” (bk. İsrâ 17/86)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r6.claim: The authors prefer reading the exception, as in 76:30, as a general divine principle: God creates and equips people for their purpose, enabling thought, speech, memory, and forgetting; the Prophet forgets nothing recited because God wills it, though He could will otherwise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:6/r6.anchor: Kulunu yaratılış amacına uygun olarak şekillendiren ve donatan Allah’tır. O böyle yapmasaydı insan böyle olmazdı
